_note: 대비 강세(contrastive stress) 문항. 같은 문장이라도 어느 단어에 강세가 오느냐로 뜻이 달라진다.
설계 원칙: 오답 3개는 '다른 단어에 강세가 왔을 때의 뜻'으로 만든다.
그래야 스크립트만 읽어서는 절대 풀 수 없고, 강세를 들어야만 답이 나온다.
...가 강세 위치이며 build_listening.py가 로 바꾼다.

turns.t: We're meeting at the library on Thursday.

choices: The day of the meeting
The place of the meeting
Who is coming to the meeting
The time the meeting starts
items.transcriptMarked: We're meeting at the library on **THURSDAY**.  ← 요일에 강세
items.explanation: 'Thursday'에 강세가 있으므로 대조되는 것은 '다른 요일'이다. 장소를 바로잡는 것이었다면 'library'에 강세가 왔을 것.

turns.t: We're meeting at the library on Thursday.

choices: The place of the meeting
The day of the meeting
Who is coming to the meeting
Whether the meeting will happen
items.transcriptMarked: We're meeting at the **LIBRARY** on Thursday.  ← 장소에 강세
items.explanation: 앞 문항과 글자는 똑같지만 강세가 'library'로 옮겨졌다. 따라서 바로잡는 것은 장소이고, 요일은 문제가 아니다.

turns.t: Jenny brought the cookies to the party.

items.stem: What does the speaker's stress suggest?
choices: Jenny brought something other than cookies
Jenny took the cookies somewhere else
Someone thought a different person brought them
Jenny did not go to the party
items.transcriptMarked: **JENNY** brought the cookies to the party.  ← 사람 이름에 강세
items.explanation: 주어에 강세가 놓이면 '다른 사람이 아니라 바로 그 사람'이라는 대조가 된다. 가져온 물건을 바로잡는 것이었다면 'cookies'에 강세가 왔을 것.

turns.t: Jenny brought the cookies to the party.

items.stem: What does the speaker's stress suggest?
choices: Jenny was expected to bring something else
A different person brought the cookies
Jenny arrived late to the party
The party was held somewhere else
items.transcriptMarked: Jenny brought the **COOKIES** to the party.  ← 물건에 강세
items.explanation: 목적어에 강세가 오면 '다른 것이 아니라 이것'이라는 뜻이다. 사람을 바로잡는 것이었다면 'Jenny'에 강세가 왔을 것.

turns.t: I never said the test was easy.

choices: Someone else called the test easy
He said something else about the test
He never mentioned the test at all
He was talking about a different test
items.transcriptMarked: I never said the test was **EASY**.  ← 'easy'에 강세
items.explanation: 'easy'에 강세가 있으므로 시험 얘기는 했지만 '쉽다'고는 안 했다는 뜻이다. 'I'에 강세였다면 '다른 사람이 그렇게 말했다', 'said'에 강세였다면 '생각은 했지만 입 밖에 내진 않았다'가 된다.

turns.t: I never said the test was easy.

choices: He said something else about the test
Someone else said that, not him
He thought it but did not say it
He does not remember the test
items.transcriptMarked: **I** never said the test was easy.  ← 'I'에 강세
items.explanation: 주어에 강세가 오면 '내가 아니라 다른 사람'이라는 대조다. 같은 문장이라도 강세가 'easy'에 있었다면 뜻이 완전히 달라진다.

turns.t: He told me to wait here.

choices: The exact place he was told to wait
Who gave him the instruction
How long he has to wait
That he was told, not asked
items.transcriptMarked: He told me to wait **HERE**.  ← 장소 부사에 강세
items.explanation: 장소를 나타내는 'here'에 강세가 있으므로 '다른 데가 아니라 바로 여기'라는 뜻이다.

turns.t: The homework is due tomorrow.

items.stem: What does the speaker's stress suggest?
choices: A different assignment is due
The homework is optional
Someone was wrong about the deadline
The homework was already collected
items.transcriptMarked: The homework is due **TOMORROW**.  ← 기한에 강세
items.explanation: 기한을 나타내는 단어에 강세가 놓이면 대개 상대가 잘못 알고 있는 날짜를 바로잡는 것이다.

turns.t: My sister borrowed my jacket.

items.stem: What is the speaker pointing out?
choices: Her sister took it without asking
Her sister borrowed it, not bought it
It was her jacket, not someone else's
Her sister took a jacket, not a coat
items.transcriptMarked: My sister borrowed **MY** jacket.  ← 소유격에 강세
items.explanation: 소유격에 강세가 오면 '누구의 것인가'가 초점이다. 빌린 행위 자체가 초점이었다면 'borrowed'에 강세가 왔을 것.

turns.t: My sister borrowed my jacket.

items.stem: What is the speaker pointing out?
choices: It was hers, not her sister's
It will be returned - it was not taken for good
Her sister, not someone else, took it
The jacket was new
items.transcriptMarked: My sister **BORROWED** my jacket.  ← 동사에 강세
items.explanation: 동사에 강세가 오면 행위의 성격이 초점이다. 'borrow(빌리다)'를 강조하면 '가져가 버린 게 아니라 빌린 것'이라는 뜻이 된다.

turns.t: We walked to school this morning.

choices: They went on foot rather than by bus or car
They went to school, not somewhere else
They went this morning, not yesterday
Only some of them went to school
items.transcriptMarked: We **WALKED** to school this morning.  ← 동사에 강세
items.explanation: 이동 방법을 나타내는 동사에 강세가 놓였으므로 '다른 수단이 아니라 걸어서'라는 대조가 된다.

turns.t: I put your lunch in the fridge.

items.stem: Why does the speaker stress that word?
choices: To say whose lunch it is
To say where to find it
To say what the food is
To say who put it there
items.transcriptMarked: I put your lunch in the **FRIDGE**.  ← 장소에 강세
items.explanation: 장소 명사에 강세가 있으면 '어디에 있는지'가 핵심 정보다. 아마 상대가 다른 곳을 찾고 있었을 것이다.

turns.t: She's not coming to the concert tonight.

items.stem: What can be understood from the stress?
choices: She dislikes concerts in general
Someone else is coming instead
The concert has been canceled
She may come to a different concert another time
items.transcriptMarked: She's not coming to the concert **TONIGHT**.  ← 시점에 강세
items.explanation: 부정문에서 시점에 강세가 오면 부정의 범위가 그 시점으로 좁혀진다. 즉 '오늘 밤은 안 오지만 다른 때는 올 수도'라는 뜻이 된다.

turns.t: We can't leave until everyone is ready.

choices: They will leave very soon
They cannot leave at all today
Being ready is not important
No one may be left behind
items.transcriptMarked: We can't leave until **EVERYONE** is ready.  ← 'everyone'에 강세
items.explanation: 'everyone'에 강세를 주면 '한 사람도 빠짐없이'라는 뜻이 강조된다. 대부분이 준비된 것으로는 부족하다는 의미.

turns.t: They finished the project without any help.

items.stem: What does the stress add to the sentence?
choices: That the project was difficult
That they wanted help but got none
That the project is not finished yet
That they had absolutely no help at all
items.transcriptMarked: They finished the project without **ANY** help.  ← 'any'에 강세
items.explanation: 부정어와 함께 쓰인 'any'에 강세를 주면 '조금도 없었다'는 완전 부정이 강조된다. 놀라움이나 감탄이 담긴다.

turns.t: That's not what I meant.

choices: She does not understand the question
She changed her mind about it
Someone else may have meant that, but she did not
She agrees with what was said
items.transcriptMarked: That's not what **I** meant.  ← 'I'에 강세
items.explanation: 'I'에 강세를 주면 '내 뜻은 그게 아니다 — 그렇게 말한 건 다른 사람'이라는 대조가 생긴다. 'meant'에 강세였다면 단순히 '오해했다'는 뜻에 그친다.

turns.t: You should have told me earlier.

choices: He was told by the wrong person
The problem was the timing, not the telling
He was never told at all
He does not want to hear about it
items.transcriptMarked: You should have told me **EARLIER**.  ← 시점 부사에 강세
items.explanation: 'earlier'에 강세가 오므로 말한 것 자체는 문제가 아니고 '더 일찍 했어야 했다'는 시점이 초점이다.

turns.t: The teacher gave us three examples.

choices: Because the number is being corrected
Because the examples were difficult
Because a different teacher gave them
Because the examples were not helpful
items.transcriptMarked: The teacher gave us **THREE** examples.  ← 숫자에 강세
items.explanation: 숫자에 강세가 놓이면 대개 상대가 잘못 기억한 개수를 바로잡는 것이다.

turns.t: I can hear the music from my room.

items.stem: What does the speaker most likely mean?
choices: The music is coming from another room
He wants the music turned up
He can hear it even if he cannot see it
He is listening in his own room
items.transcriptMarked: I can **HEAR** the music from my room.  ← 지각동사에 강세
items.explanation: 감각을 나타내는 동사에 강세가 오면 다른 감각과의 대조가 생긴다. 여기서는 '보이지는 않아도 들린다'는 뜻.

turns.t: I borrowed the book from the library.

items.stem: What is the speaker making clear?
choices: She went to the library, not a bookstore
She took a book, not a magazine
She went there by herself
She did not buy or keep the book
items.transcriptMarked: I **BORROWED** the book from the library.  ← 동사에 강세
items.explanation: 동사에 강세를 주어 행위의 성격을 분명히 한다 — 사거나 가진 게 아니라 빌린 것이다.

turns.t: She wants to study science in college.

items.stem: What does the stress tell you?
choices: She is not sure about her plan
She will study somewhere far away
She has already started studying
The subject is what matters here
items.transcriptMarked: She wants to study **SCIENCE** in college.  ← 과목에 강세
items.explanation: 과목 이름에 강세가 놓였으므로 '다른 전공이 아니라 과학'이라는 점이 초점이다.

turns.t: He said the answer was on page ten.

choices: Who gave the information
Whether there is an answer
Which book to look in
Which page number it is
items.transcriptMarked: He said the answer was on page **TEN**.  ← 쪽수에 강세
items.explanation: 쪽수에 강세가 있으므로 다른 쪽을 보고 있는 상대를 바로잡는 것이다.

turns.t: My brother doesn't like spicy food.

items.stem: What can be understood from the stress?
choices: Her brother dislikes all food
Her brother has never tried spicy food
She does not like spicy food either
Other people in the family do like it
items.transcriptMarked: My **BROTHER** doesn't like spicy food.  ← 주어에 강세
items.explanation: 부정문의 주어에 강세를 주면 '그 사람만 그렇다'는 대조가 생겨, 나머지는 반대라는 뜻이 함께 전달된다.

turns.t: The meeting starts at two thirty.

choices: The hour of the meeting
The minutes past the hour
The day of the meeting
Where the meeting is held
items.transcriptMarked: The meeting starts at two **THIRTY**.  ← 분에 강세
items.explanation: 'two'가 아니라 'thirty'에 강세가 있으므로 시(hour)가 아니라 분을 바로잡는 것이다. 아마 상대가 2시로 알고 있었을 것.

turns.t: I already told her about the change.

choices: He told the wrong person
He will tell her soon
There is no need to tell her again
He forgot to tell her
items.transcriptMarked: I **ALREADY** told her about the change.  ← 'already'에 강세
items.explanation: 'already'를 강조하면 '이미 끝난 일이니 또 할 필요 없다'는 뜻이 된다. 살짝 답답함이 묻어나기도 한다.

turns.t: You can borrow mine if you need one.

choices: That she needs one too
That she is offering her own
That borrowing is not allowed
That she will buy a new one
items.transcriptMarked: You can borrow **MINE** if you need one.  ← 소유대명사에 강세
items.explanation: 소유대명사에 강세를 주면 '남의 것이 아니라 내 것'을 빌려주겠다는 제안이 분명해진다.

turns.t: I only had one question about your essay.

choices: The essay had many problems
She did not read the essay
She wants the essay rewritten
She had just a single small concern
items.transcriptMarked: I only had **ONE** question about your essay.  ← 수량에 강세
items.explanation: 'only'와 함께 숫자에 강세를 주면 '그만큼 적다'가 강조된다. 즉 대체로 잘 썼다는 긍정적 신호에 가깝다.

turns.t: I thought you were going to call me.

choices: He forgot to make the call himself
He does not have the phone number
He called but no one answered
He expected the other person to call
items.transcriptMarked: I thought **YOU** were going to call me.  ← 'you'에 강세
items.explanation: 'you'에 강세가 오면 '전화할 사람은 내가 아니라 너였다'는 책임 소재의 대조가 된다. 가벼운 항의가 담긴다.
